title: Fractions: Division, Operators and Simplest Form
kicker: Cambridge Primary Checkpoint · Mathematics 0096 · Stage 6 · Number
summary: See every fraction as a division, find fractions of amounts with proper and improper fractions, and write fractions in their simplest form — with bar models, worked examples and a Checkpoint-style quiz.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Understand that a fraction is the numerator divided by the denominator — for proper and improper fractions (6Nf.01)
Understand that proper and improper fractions can act as operators: find 3/5 of 40 or 7/4 of 12 (6Nf.02)
Use equivalent fractions to write fractions in their simplest form (6Nf.03)

blocks.text: Key words

items: numerator
البسط — the top number: how many parts you have
denominator
المقام — the bottom number: how many equal parts make one whole
proper fraction
كسر حقيقي — numerator smaller than denominator, worth less than 1: 3/4
improper fraction
كسر غير حقيقي — numerator equal to or bigger than denominator, worth 1 or more: 7/4
mixed number
عدد كسري — a whole number and a proper fraction: 1 3/4 (one and three-quarters)
operator
مؤثر / عملية — a fraction that acts on a number: 3/5 of 40 means 3/5 × 40
equivalent fractions
كسور متكافئة — fractions with the same value: 3/4 = 6/8
simplest form
أبسط صورة — numerator and denominator have no common factor except 1
common factor
عامل مشترك — a number that divides both numbers exactly
highest common factor (HCF)
العامل المشترك الأكبر — the biggest common factor

blocks.text: 1. A fraction is a division
The fraction line means **divide**. So 3/4 means 3 ÷ 4, and 3 ÷ 4 can be written as 3/4. The numerator is the number being shared; the denominator is the number of equal shares.

blocks.text: **Improper fractions to mixed numbers.** Because 17/5 means 17 ÷ 5, divide: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2. The 3 is the whole number and the remainder 2 is still to be shared by 5, so 17/5 = **3 2/5** (three and two-fifths).
**Mixed numbers to improper fractions.** Reverse it: 3 2/5 = (3 × 5 + 2)/5 = 17/5.
**Remainders as fractions.** Sharing 22 metres of rope between 5 people: 22 ÷ 5 = 22/5 = 4 2/5 metres each. The remainder 2 is divided by 5 too.
2. Fractions as operators: "a fraction of a number"
In maths, **of** means **multiply**. 3/5 of 40 means 3/5 × 40. The fraction is an **operator** — it does something to the number.

items: Divide the number by the **denominator** to find one part (40 ÷ 5 = 8).
Multiply by the **numerator** to find the parts you need (8 × 3 = 24).

blocks.text: **Working backwards.** If 2/3 of a number is 18, then 1/3 of it is 18 ÷ 2 = 9, and the whole number (3/3) is 9 × 3 = 27. Divide by the numerator to find one part, then multiply by the denominator.
3. Equivalent fractions and simplest form
Equivalent fractions have the **same value**. You make them by multiplying (or dividing) the numerator **and** the denominator by the **same** number.

blocks.text: 3/4 = 6/8 (× 2 top and bottom) = 9/12 (× 3 top and bottom). Going the other way, dividing top and bottom by a common factor, **simplifies** the fraction.
**Method — writing a fraction in its simplest form:**

items: Find a common factor of the numerator and denominator (try 2, 3, 5 … or use your times tables).
Divide both by it.
Repeat until the only common factor is 1. (Quicker: divide by the highest common factor in one step.)
Check: can any number except 1 divide both? If not, you are finished.

rows: 7 and 12 have no common factor except 1

blocks.text: **Missing numbers.** 4/5 = ☐/35: the denominator was multiplied by 7 (5 × 7 = 35), so multiply the numerator by 7 too: 4 × 7 = 28. So 4/5 = 28/35.

blocks.title: افتكر القاعدة دي
items: خط الكسر معناه «قسمة»: ٣/٤ = ٣ ÷ ٤. يعني ٣ بيتزا بين ٤ أشخاص = كل واحد ٣/٤.
«٣/٥ من ٤٠» = اقسم على المقام (٤٠ ÷ ٥ = ٨) وبعدين اضرب في البسط (٨ × ٣ = ٢٤). لو الكسر أكبر من ١ الناتج هيطلع أكبر من العدد.
أبسط صورة: اقسم البسط والمقام على نفس العدد لحد ما مايبقاش فيه عامل مشترك غير ١.

blocks.text: Worked examples
**Worked example 1** — 4 friends share 3 pizzas equally. What fraction of a pizza does each friend get? [1 mark]
Sharing means dividing: 3 ÷ 4 = **3/4** of a pizza. **Common mistake:** writing 4/3 — the number being shared (3 pizzas) goes on top.
**Worked example 2** — Write 23/6 as a mixed number. [1 mark]
23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5 (because 3 × 6 = 18 and 23 − 18 = 5). The remainder is still divided by 6: **3 5/6**. **Check:** 3 × 6 + 5 = 23 ✓.
**Worked example 3** — Work out (a) 5/8 of 56 (b) 9/4 of 20. [2 marks]

items: (b) 20 ÷ 4 = 5, then 5 × 9 = **45**. The answer is more than 20 because 9/4 is more than 1 whole.

blocks.text: **Worked example 4** — Write 42/56 in its simplest form. [1 mark]

Both are in the 7 times table: 42 ÷ 7 = 6 and 56 ÷ 7 = 8, giving 6/8. 6 and 8 are both even: ÷ 2 gives **3/4**. (The HCF of 42 and 56 is 14, so ÷ 14 does it in one step.) **Common mistake:** stopping at 6/8 — check again for a common factor.
**Worked example 5** — Hana has 60 stickers. She gives 2/5 of them to her brother. Then she gives 1/4 of the stickers she has left to her friend. How many stickers does Hana keep? [2 marks]

items: 2/5 of 60: 60 ÷ 5 = 12, 12 × 2 = 24 given to her brother.
1/4 of 36 = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 given to her friend.
Keeps 36 − 9 = **27** stickers.

blocks.text: **Common mistake:** finding 1/4 of 60 instead of 1/4 of the stickers that are **left**. Underline "the rest" or "left" in the question. (A method mark is usually given for 24 or 36 seen.)
**Worked example 6** — 3/4 of a number is 27. What is the number? [1 mark]
3 quarters = 27, so 1 quarter = 27 ÷ 3 = 9. The whole = 4 quarters = 9 × 4 = **36**. **Check:** 3/4 of 36 = 36 ÷ 4 × 3 = 27 ✓.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Writing the division the wrong way round: 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4, not 4/3.
For "3/5 of 40", dividing by the numerator and multiplying by the denominator. Divide by the **bottom**, multiply by the **top**.
Thinking a fraction of a number is always smaller. With an improper fraction (7/4 of 12) the answer is bigger.
Changing only the numerator or only the denominator when making equivalent fractions.
Adding or subtracting the same number top and bottom: 3/4 is not equal to 4/5.
Not simplifying fully: 6/8 is not the simplest form of 42/56 — 3/4 is.

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: "Write 5 ÷ 8 as a fraction" or "Which fraction is equal to 9 ÷ 4? Ring it."
Sharing stories: "7 cakes are shared equally between 3 children…" — write numerator ÷ denominator.
"Work out 3/5 of 45" in a box, often with an improper fraction to check you understand the answer can be bigger.
Multi-step word problems ("… of the rest"): show each step so you can get a method mark.
"Write 18/24 in its simplest form" — the answer must be fully simplified for the mark.
"Tick the fraction that is in its simplest form" or matching equivalent fractions with lines.
Missing-number equivalences: 4/5 = ☐/35 or 12/☐ = 3/4.

blocks.text: Practice

blocks.title: Fractions — practice
blocks.intro: 14 questions, from easy to Checkpoint-hard. No calculator. Type fractions like 3/4 and mixed numbers like 3 2/5 (whole number, space, fraction). For the explain question, mark yourself with the mark scheme.

questions.e: 9 ÷ 4 = 9/4 (= 2 1/4). 4/9 is the division the wrong way round; 1 1/4 = 5/4 and 3/4 are not equal to 9/4.

questions.q: 5 pizzas are shared equally between 8 children. What fraction of a pizza does each child get?
questions.e: Sharing is dividing: 5 ÷ 8 = 5/8 of a pizza each.
20 ÷ 4 = 5, then 5 × 7 = 35. The answer is more than 20 because 7/4 is more than 1.

questions.q: Which of these has the largest answer?
There are 30 children in a class. 2/5 of them are boys. How many girls are in the class?
questions.e: Boys: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12. Girls: 30 − 12 = 18. (Or girls are 3/5: 6 × 3 = 18.) 1 mark for 12 boys seen.

questions.q: 2/3 of a number is 18. What is the number?
questions.e: 2 thirds = 18, so 1 third = 18 ÷ 2 = 9. The whole = 3 thirds = 9 × 3 = 27. Check: 2/3 of 27 = 18 ✓.
The HCF of 18 and 24 is 6: 18 ÷ 6 = 3, 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Simplest form 3/4. (9/12 or 6/8 are equivalent but not fully simplified.)

questions.q: Which fraction is in its simplest form?
questions.e: 7 and 12 have no common factor except 1, so 7/12 is in simplest form. 6/9 = 2/3 (÷ 3), 10/15 = 2/3 (÷ 5), 14/21 = 2/3 (÷ 7).
5 × 7 = 35, so multiply the numerator by 7 too: 4 × 7 = 28. 4/5 = 28/35.

questions.q: Which is 15 ÷ 6 written as a fraction in its simplest form?
questions.e: 15 ÷ 6 = 15/6. The HCF of 15 and 6 is 3: 15/6 = 5/2. (15/6 is correct but not in simplest form; 6/15 and 2/5 are the wrong way round.)

questions.q: Explain why 12/16 and 15/20 are equivalent fractions.
questions.ms: 1 mark: shows both simplify to 3/4, e.g. 12/16 = 3/4 (÷ 4) and 15/20 = 3/4 (÷ 5); or both have the same value 0.75 / 75%; or converts both to a common denominator (e.g. 60/80 and 60/80). Do not accept 'because both numerators and denominators are 4 apart'.
questions.e: 12/16: divide top and bottom by 4 → 3/4. 15/20: divide top and bottom by 5 → 3/4. Both are equal to 3/4, so they are equivalent.

blocks.title: Remember
items: A fraction is a division: a/b = a ÷ b. 3 shared by 4 = 3/4 each.
Improper → mixed: divide (17 ÷ 5 = 3 r 2 → 3 2/5). Mixed → improper: whole × denominator + numerator.
Fraction of a number: ÷ by the denominator, × by the numerator. Improper fractions give a bigger answer.
Equivalent fractions: × or ÷ top and bottom by the same number.
Simplest form: divide by common factors (best: the HCF) until only 1 is left in common.
